chunks: When the idolaters see their partners they will call out: 'O our Lord, these are the partners we invoked instead of You;' but they will retort: 'You are liars.'
ai.seo_question: What do the idols say to the polytheists on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In this verse from Surah An-Nahl, the polytheists (mushrikun) present their idols as intercessors on the Day of Judgment, only to be rejected by them as false claims. This mutual denial underscores the Shia scholarly understanding of *Tawhid* by illustrating that created entities possess no independent power to intercede, thereby nullifying the concept of *Shirk* as a valid spiritual connection. The scene serves as a practical warning against attributing divine qualities to beings other than Allah, emphasizing that true intercession belongs solely to Him by His permission.
